headline: The ledger, first run and the new screens hold up: RLS is tight, balances match hand-worked figures, and 112 of 113 breakage checks die. One Major: no test guards the offline copy's paging across tables. Six Minors (words, a field error in a toast, a placeholder, a stale tree, an unexplained flag, apps chosen after first run get no account).

suites.qa-e2e: b08r3: 8 specs, 7 pass, 1 fails on finding 2

findings.title: No test pages the offline copy past one page: a breakage there survives
findings.detail: `/sync/changes` pages across five tables by one counter (D146 (9)): a page ends at the 500th lowest version across all of them. Replacing that with the highest version seen (`const top = all.at(-1) ?? since`) skips, for good, every row of a table that had more than a page left: the phone's offline copy (categories for the category prompt, account names for B09) silently misses rows. No suite noticed. The code is right today: I paged a person with 600 categories, 2 accounts and 300 account names and got all 902 rows exactly once (v 672 more true, then v 1075 more false). The guard is what's missing: the only paging assertions check `more: false`.

findings.title: Accounts says “In 1 accounts”
findings.detail: With one tracked account the line over the total reads *In 1 accounts*. The common first-run case for a friend with one bank. `accounts.tsx`: `In {v.tracked.length} accounts`.
findings.repro: Sign in as a person with one account; open More → Accounts
findings.evidence: Locator: getByText('In 1 account', { exact: true }) — element(s) not found; screen shows 'In 1 accounts'

findings.title: A taken category name lands in a toast over the sheet, not under the Name field
findings.detail: Renaming (or adding) a category to a name in use: the API answers 409 `{code:name_taken, field:"name"}`, but the sheet shows nothing at the field; the words arrive as a toast that covers the *Discretionary* switch. patterns.md §7 *Forms*: a Field's message below it. The field isn't marked invalid, so a screen reader hears nothing at the field.
findings.repro: Settings → Categories → Groceries → rename to *Market*, Save; open Market → type *meals* → Save
findings.evidence: Toast 'You already have a category with that name.'; field-error elements with that text: 0

findings.title: First run's empty balances show “RM 0.00” beside “Type today’s balance, or 0.”
findings.detail: On the accounts step an empty field shows a large slate-grey *RM 0.00* placeholder. Tapping Next with nothing typed puts *Type today’s balance, or 0.* under each, while each already seems to say 0.00. A person with an empty GrabPay is told to type what they see. Run 1 fixed the same class on the name and payday fields (placeholders that read as values); this one stayed.
findings.repro: First run to step 5; tap Next with nothing typed
findings.evidence: 4 × 'Type today’s balance, or 0.' under four fields each showing RM 0.00 (placeholder)

findings.title: balance-check's committed tree is stale; pnpm e2e passed over it
findings.detail: The diff run rewrote `apps/web/e2e/trees/balance-check.aria.yml`: the committed tree lacks D147 (3)'s *what it holds* lines (`Main account and pockets together`, `eWallet and GO+ together`). `pnpm e2e` passed 1415/1415 against it, so the tree match takes a regex as a prefix: text added after it goes unnoticed (run 2 saw the same with a dropped placeholder). The rewrite is left uncommitted for the parent.
findings.evidence:
-        - paragraph: /Ryt Bank Sen has RM \d+,\d+\.\d+/
+        - paragraph: /Ryt Bank Sen has RM \d+,\d+\.\d+ Main account and pockets together/

findings.title: More → Accounts settles 0.4 s later than main in the harness; the cause isn't found
findings.detail: Metrics flag step:balance-check/1 (and first-run/20, the same tap). Re-run in the harness, 3 each: head 816, 864, 869 ms; main 446, 468, 511 ms; the filmstrip shows the list skeleton for the whole second. Outside the harness, on the same two builds with the service worker, the CPU 4× slower and the same network: time to the total 524–586 ms on head, 550–706 ms on main, last DOM change 476–627 against 490–550 ms, no change after the content (4 runs each). So the harness sees something my probe doesn't. Unexplained flags are findings: what the harness counts after the content needs naming.
findings.repro: QA_SERVE=head|base … playwright test -c e2e/diff.config.ts e2e/journeys.spec.ts --project metrics-<side> -g balance-check --repeat-each 3; qa/e2e/b08r3-accounts-open.probe.mjs

probe head: content 579/536/565/666 ms; base 604/603/558/540 ms

findings.title: An app chosen after first run never gets an account, and there's no way to add one
findings.detail: D145: each chosen app feeds exactly one tracked account. Accounts are only made at first run's step 5 (`account.add` has no other caller). Choosing TNG, Public Bank and Grab later in Settings → Capture leaves the person with 1 account and no *Add* on Accounts. B09 will capture payments from those apps with no account to book them to. The spec is silent on when such an app's account is made: an open question for the owner, beside run 2's note 13 (un-chosen apps).
findings.repro: Finish first run with one app; Settings → Capture → apps → Choose these 4; open Accounts
findings.evidence: DB accounts for the person: 1; Accounts: 'In 1 accounts', add buttons: 0

findings.title: A numeric opening balance written straight to the database is rounded, not refused
findings.detail: `INSERT … opening_balance = 10.5` stores 11 (Postgres's assignment cast). Only the API writes accounts, and zod refuses non-integers, so nothing reaches it today; a CHECK can't catch it either. Recorded for the agent's tools later.
findings.repro: psql as app_user: insert into accounts(…, opening_balance) values (…, 10.5)

findings.title: The API accepts a negative opening balance
findings.detail: `account.add` with opening −500 → 200 (`Sen` allows ±MAX_SEN). The phone can't type a minus. Whether an account can open below zero (an overdraft) isn't in the spec: an open question.

findings.title: A retried account.add with different content says it added the new name
findings.detail: Same id, a new name: answers *Changed added* while the row keeps *Grab* (correctly a no-op). The words describe what wasn't done.
findings.repro: account.add id d0…01 name Grab, then the same id with name Changed

findings.title: A category name may hold a right-to-left override
findings.detail: `\u202eslaeM` is saved and shows as *Meals* reversed in the person's own list. Self-only, no reach to others.
